title: Deal Signals & Contract Quickplay (personal scratch)
content:
Quick, dirty scratchpad for contract redlines — keep this terse, copy bits into redlines and playbook. Notes to self and rapid counters for common sticks we see.

PRIORITY: protect platform liability, avoid indemnity expanses, lock data boundaries. Rank order: 1) Liability cap + exclusions 2) Data/PHI/PII carveouts & breach timing 3) Audit & access 4) SLA credits, rollback/escape 5) IP/outputs rules and model weight usage 6) Subprocessors & flow-downs.

Red flags to flag immediately (first-pass):
- Unlimited indemnity asks (patent/third-party claims ok if narrow; everything else — push back).
- Customer tries to make us indemnify for regulatory fines or statutory penalties.
- Carrier/insurance threshold < our cap -- reconcile with finance.
- Retroactive data ownership claims or assignment of customer-generated content as Redwood IP.
- Broad audit rights (eg. onsite, continuous) without scope/notice and cost-sharing.
- SLA that allows termination for failure to meet trivial uptime thresholds.
- Termination-for-convenience with high break fees or no transition assistance.
- Broad liability carveouts for "indirect" that then attempts to bring in consequential by definition.

Quick counters / playbook language (short):
- Liability cap: "Each party’s aggregate liability shall not exceed the fees paid under the applicable Order in the prior 12 months; for claims arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, cap is the greater of $1M or fees paid in prior 12 months."
- Exclusions: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party excludes liability for (i) death or bodily injury resulting from negligence, (ii) fraud, or (iii) breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations."
- Indemnity (third-party IP): "Provider will defend and indemnify Customer for third-party IP infringement claims to the extent that such claim arises solely from Provider’s model implementation; Provider’s indemnity is subject to Customer (a) notifying Provider promptly, (b) allowing Provider to control defense and settlement, and (c) not admitting liability without Provider consent."
- Data breach / notice: "Provider to notify Customer within 72 hours of becoming aware of a confirmed breach affecting Customer Data; provide remediation plan and cooperation. Provider’s breach notification obligations limited to incidents directly caused by Provider’s systems, not Customer misconfiguration."
- Audit: "Customer may request documentation and remote evidence up to once per 12 months. Onsite audits require 60 days’ notice, mutually agreeable scope, and Customer bears reasonable costs if findings are not Provider-responsible."
- SLA credits: "Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for unavailability. Termination right only if downtime > 3 consecutive months or repeated missed SLOs after 2 remediation periods."
- Termination assistance: "Provider to provide export of Customer Data and reasonable transition assistance for up to 90 days; additional assistance at provider’s then-current professional services rates."

Data / privacy heuristics (short checklist):
- Distinguish Customer Data (ingested prompts, settings) vs Derived Outputs vs Model Weights. Never cede rights to model weights.
- Push back on any clause that says we "own" or "may use" Customer Data for model training by default — require opt-in and explicit terms plus anonymization and deletion TTLs.
- If HIPAA/PHI is in-scope: add BAA and clarify breach reporting 24 hours, dedicated contacts, SOC2 plus penetration test cadence.
- Cross-border transfers: require Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent. No surprise offshore subprocessors without notice.

Negotiation tactics / playbook bullets (notes to self):
- Start with narrow counters: limit indemnity scope, propose numeric cap anchored to MRR or prior 12 months fees.
- If customer insists on broader indemnity, request insurer endorsement and carveouts for negligence by customer or third parties.
- Trade: reduced liability cap only in exchange for higher committed spend (dedicated) or multi-year term + escrow.
- Use canary language: allow demo/POC exceptions with strict timebox and no training rights.
- Always insert rollback/exit assistance clause when termination for convenience allowed.

Walkaway triggers (hard stop):
- Customer demands transfer of our IP (model weights, infra code) as part of standard contract.
- Unlimited liability for data/privacy or regulatory fines without insurance/mitigation.
- Obligation to indemnify third-party claims where Provider had no control and no right to defend.

Deal-specific notes (scratch for current negotiation):
- Customer: fintech-scale startup; wants training rights + model custody. Push: deny training rights; propose pseudonymized telemetry share + audited metrics instead.
- SLA ask: 99.95% for gen endpoints 24/7. Agree for committed Dedicated pool; for hosted API propose 99.9% and credits.
- Audit: Customer wants monthly logs + ability to pull raw request/response. Limit to metadata and aggregated logs; raw PII only via eDiscovery with warrant/legal process.
- Data residency: wants EU-only. If Dedicated not available in region, offer encryption-in-transit+at-rest + SCCs + customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms) as compromise.

Scripted talking points (one-liners to use in negotiation):
- "We can commit to transparent metrics and regular reporting, but ownership of our models and kernels is non-negotiable — this is core IP that enables predictable performance."
- "Liability mirrors commercial risk: for routine availability and service issues, credits are the practical remedy and proportional to impact."
- "Training on customer data requires explicit opt-in; we treat customer inputs as confidential and will only use them with consent and technical safeguards."

Unresolved questions / flags to research:
- Confirm with finance the absolute minimum insurance endorsement language we can accept (carrier, additional insured?).
- Ask infra if we can guarantee per-tenant encryption keys for this customer (BYOK) and what ops cost looks like.
- Validate how long we can keep rollback snapshots for Dedicated customers without incurring storage costs that need to be charged back.

Copy-able snippets (save to templates later):
- "Provider shall not be required to indemnify for claims arising from (a) Customer content that violates law; (b) Customer use outside documented API; (c) combination with third-party products not approved by Provider."
- "Any customer request for production access to Provider model weights or raw weights/dump will be treated as a separate professional services engagement and is not part of this Agreement."

Final mnemonic to keep top of mind: LIDA — Liability, Indemnity, Data, Audit. Run through LIDA on every redline.

Notes-to-self: paste into ticket JIRA-LEGAL-101 when cleaning up final counters. If stuck, escalate to Maya for indemnity carveouts negotiation. Keep this doc short and portable — it's a personal quickplay, not the canonical playbook.
